newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss govt says initial 1998 deficit 8.7 bln Sfr.
newsitem.headline: Swiss govt says initial 1998 deficit 8.7 bln Sfr.

text.p: The Swiss government, fighting to cap rising federal debt, on Monday said an initial and unrevised draft of 1998 spending showed a deficit of 8.7 billion Swiss francs after 5.7 billion planned for 1997.

In a statement after a cabinet meeting, Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger said projected deficits must be cut by at least one billion and 1.5 billion Swiss francs next year and between two billion and four billion from 1999 until 2001.

Villiger said the cabinet had ordered his ministry to come up with a rigorous savings plan for 1998 by autumn, when the government will present its final budget draft for next year to parliament for approval.
The cabinet also approved a proposed anti-deficit article for the constitution, passing it to parliament for consideration in its autumn session.
The amendment would set an interim deficit goal of no more than four billion Swiss francs in 1999 and a final target of two percent of revenue or around one billion Swiss francs in 2001.
If those goals were not met, the article would require government and parliament by law to cut the budget further.
